UNIVERSITY OF LIMPOPO’S VISION STATEMENT
“To be a leading African University focused on the developmental needs of its communities and
epitomising academic excellence and innovativeness.”
UNIVERSITY OF LIMPOPO’S MISSION STATEMENT
• We provide excellent and relevant academic programmes, research and
• community engagement initiatives which respond to the developmental
• needs of communities whilst producing well rounded graduates who give back to their communities
and are global citizens.
• We enhance access to higher education for under-prepared, socially and economically disadvantaged
students in particular.
• We provide academic support services to all students at the University in order to ensure success in
their studies.
• We provide planned opportunities for the development of all staff, particularly the academic staff in
respect of their teaching, research and community engagement skills.
• We strive to strengthen and maintain partnerships and collaboration with the government and private
sector, local authorities, international institutions and our alumni community.
• We endeavour to diversify the University’s funding streams significantly,
• particularly the increase of third-stream income, in order to support the launching of new teaching and
learning, research and community engagement activities and sustain the existing ones.
UNIVERSITY OF LIMPOPO’S MOTTO
“Finding Solutions for Africa.”

Welcome Message
The University warmly welcomes your interest in advancing your postgraduate education with us. In line with
our vision, pursuing a postgraduate degree is not only about personal growth and development, but also
about making significant social and economic contributions to society.
A postgraduate qualification does more than give you a competitive edge in your career. It is a personally

rewarding and prestigious achievement. Starting your journey at the Honours or Postgraduate Diploma level
opens doors for career progression, allows for specialisation in your chosen field, and sparks an interest in
research and lifelong learning.

As you advance to the Masters and Doctoral levels, you will further deepen your specialised knowledge and
skills, thereby enhanci ng your competitiveness in your career. You will also develop the proficiency to
conduct impactful research projects, contributing to the body of knowledge in your discipline and publishing
your findings in academic journals.
Moreover, postgraduate studies offer the opportunity to expand your network. Engaging with lecturers, peers,
and other professionals provides invaluable opportunities for collaboration and personal growth. Pursuing
postgraduate studies is a holistic academic journey and experience that shapes your career and contribution
towards imperatives such as human resource development strategy of the country, Sustainable
Development Goals, National Development Plan, Africa Agenda 2063 and the Millenium D evelopment
Goals.
DISCLAIMER
The University reserves the right to withdraw, add or amend any programme or any information in this
prospectus without prior notification.
The University reserves the right not to offer programmes for a particular year.
The University may only offer programmes that are accredited by the relevant professional bodies for the
year indicated.
Fulfilling the minimum admission requirements does not guarantee admission into a study programme

(degree, diploma or certificate) at the University of Limpopo. All postgraduate students will be subjected to
Departmental selection processes.

GENERAL INFORMATION
Student Selection

Meeting the admission requirements of a programme does not guarantee admission. Postgraduate
applications are subject to selection based on the number of spaces available for a programme.

Academic history provides the basis of selection at the Postgraduate Diploma and Honours levels.
For senior postgraduate programmes, selection is based on the supervisor capacity and the
availability of other appropriate resources. Additionally, the skills profile of potential students will be
assessed, and they may be required to complete additional modules or acquire competencies
deemed essential by the Department.
Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL)
The University allows for access, advanced standing and awarding of credits (for taught courses)
through RPL as per the RPL policy and General Academic Rules of the University. This applies to all
programmes, except those for which the Professional Body does not permit (please inquire with the
relevant School). RPL will be conducted a nd assessed in accordance with the University General
Academic Rules and the University of Limpopo Recognition of Prior Learning Policy. Applicants for

postgraduate studies via the RPL route must consult with the Faculty in which they intend to study.
Financial Aid

Financial aid opportunities are available for postgraduate students. The Faculty will be able to advise
you on potential funding opportunities. Potential students are also advised to contact the Financial Aid
office at the University.
Expectations for the Successful Graduation of the Work

To ensure all learning outcomes are achieved, Honours and Postgraduate Diploma/Certificate students
are expected to spend a minimum of 40 hours per week on their studies throughout the academic year.
For Master's and Doctoral Postgraduate programme student s, a minimum of 40 hours per week is
required for 45 weeks of the year for full-time study.
All Master's and Doctoral students are required to have a signed Memorandum of Understanding with
their supervisors outlining the expectations of both parties for the successful completion of their
qualification. This includes the requirement for the approval of the research proposal within 6 months
following registration.

Postgraduate Diploma in Health Promotion (PGDip (Health Promotion))
The course in Health Promotion and Education for Health aims to develop the skills of health, social
work, agriculture, education, and related workers at district, regional, provincial, and national levels,
as well as those who will be responsible for planning, implementing, and evaluating health promotion
Programmes. The course will enable participants to acquire a broad understanding of the many
facets which impact on promoting health and wellbeing, and to develop skills necessary for improving
communication betw een s ervice providers and com munities, identifying need s, pri orities, d esign
appropriate educational materials, advocate and negotiate policies to strengthen community action,
and implement empowering educational processes.
Course Design:

(a) The Postgraduate Diploma in Health Promotion is an action-learning based full-time one-year
course with six residential teaching modules for the full-time programme.
(b) Self-study segments, supported by custom-developed teaching materials, form part of both
curricula.
(c) Each residential teaching block will last for six days (Monday to Saturday).
(d) Students must undertake a project based in their work setting/agencies working in their area
of interest.
Admission Criteria:
(a) Applicants must be in possession of a B achelor’s de gree or equival ent in Health or relat ed
disciplines.
(b) Priority will be given to those who have or will have:
- The responsibility for planning, implementing and evaluating health promotion activities
at the district, regional and provincial levels.
- The r esponsibility for the promotion of heal th and well -being in dir ect liais on with the
community.
Duration
(a) One year minimum
(b) Two years maximum
